newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Credit Suisse seen abandoning gold in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Credit Suisse seen abandoning gold in Hong Kong.

text.p: Credit Suisse's gold operation in Hong Kong has stopped making markets and is no longer involved in spot or physical trading, market sources said on Tuesday.
Credit Suisse (CS) officials in Hong Kong declined to comment.
"Pricing will continue out of CS's Melbourne office," said a senior gold trader.
CS's gold department had pulled out of Hong Kong for internal reasons, market sources said.
No further details were available. According to the market sources, Credit Suisse will make a statement announcing details in the near future.
Credit Suisse would be the third company to abandon market making in Hong Kong since the beginning of September.
Local firm Sun Hung Kai said in early September it was no longer making markets as gold remained moribund. The company said it would focus on other areas instead.
Market sources also said AIG International Inc would move its gold desk from Hong Kong back to their U.S. headquarters before the end of the year.
AIG in Hong Kong denied all comment, but local gold industry sources said AIG's revenue did not justify their expenditure in the British colony.
